content.comment_body: Hello, my question might be in the wrong section. Currently I have a [product_name] and an HMI panel. I'm facing two issues. When programming buttons in the engineering software, I can only use flags from my [product_name] application—standard inputs won't work. In the HMI tag list I added physical input tags (like I0.0), but they do not function, only flag memory addresses (M0.0, etc.) work. My second issue involves the display of circles and lines: normally, changing an output from 0 to 1 lets you update a circle or line color (for example, from red to green). This does not work in my application. If I use the visibility property, outputs are detected correctly, but changing appearance does not work. I'm hoping someone can advise.

Firstly, physical digital inputs (like Ix.x) cannot be switched remotely via HMI or other devices—the [product_name] program always reads from the actual hardware inputs. For better assistance, consider uploading your complete project files from both the engineering software and logic editor as a ZIP, so we can review your implementation.

analysis.insight_summary: The user encounters challenges getting HMI buttons to control physical digital inputs on their [product_name] and HMI device setup. Only internal flags (Mx.x) are assignable, not real inputs (Ix.x), affecting expected system behavior. The user also struggles with graphical feedback—appearance changes for lines and circles based on outputs do not work, though visibility options do. These problems arise due to product architecture limitations and possibly graphics configuration in the engineering software.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects HMI buttons to connect directly to [product_name] digital inputs and wants an easy way to update graphical elements based on output status.
